setting: paper, pencil, two labeled drawings; no device, accounts or poured water
outcome: Choose and justify which differently sized container reaches half capacity first, using amount and rate rather than comparing rates alone.
misconception: The larger liters-per-minute rate always reaches halfway sooner.
storyDirection: Two young keepers at an orbital greenhouse must choose which half-full reservoir can water a fragile seedling first. A prediction should change what one keeper chooses to do. Keep the quiet speculative tone; do not turn the story into a list of teaching objectives. No dangerous actions or new facts about flow rates.
transferConstraint: Use a different surface context involving a quantity, a rate and a fractional target. Change the relationship so copying the reservoir winner does not work. Supply all numbers, a reasoned answer and scoring guidance in the facilitator portion.
access: Printed large text and optional spoken or drawn reasoning are available throughout; neither depends on a diagnostic score. Multiplication table is an optional instructional aid. Do not create learner profiles.
ordinaryQuestion: What does liters per minute mean?
